name: Solenne Atelier Lumenweft Gala Glove
description:
Opera-length evening gloves from Solenne's Spire collection, woven from bioluminescent silk-analog thread that pulses with slow, breath-synchronized light shifts — aquamarine to amber to deep violet depending on the wearer's biometric state. The weave is open enough to reveal skin underneath in a lattice pattern, making chrome hands beneath them glow through the mesh like lit sculpture.

The upper arm portion terminates in a scalloped edge weighted with micro-glass beads sourced from a dissolved Osaka atelier. Each pair is hand-finished and registered to a single client biometric profile — unauthorized wear causes the bioluminescence to go flat gray.
functionality: Bioluminescent fiber pulses with wearer's biometric rhythm; biometric lock causes flat gray response on unauthorized wearers; open lattice permits chrome hand visibility as aesthetic feature; micro-glass weighted scalloped cuff provides drape structure.
what_it_says: You are dressed by someone who knows your heartbeat, and the dress proves it.
worn_by: augmented elites using chrome as fashion statement
story_hooks: A pair appears at auction registered to a client officially listed as deceased for six months — and the bioluminescence is still active.
Someone has cracked the biometric lock on a stolen pair using a harvested pulse-spoof chip, and they're wearing them into a Spire function they have no business attending.
The Osaka micro-glass beads contain an impurity traceable to a single contaminated melt — and three separate Spire families all have gloves from that batch.
